content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'hosted-inference-prod' (INC-20260315-17). Urgency: high. Trigger: host cpu > 92% for 3m. Primary on-call: @maya paged.

maya: saw the page. jumping on now — grabbing logs and node metrics.

pd-bot: Alert timeline: primary not acknowledged within 5m → escalation to secondary @noah fired. Manager escalation policy will trigger if secondary does not ack within 10m.

noah: I got the second page. hitting the runbook. any customer-facing errors reported?

sam: monitoring dashboards show increased 5xxs on /v1/generate for region-us-west-2, error rate ~3.7% p50 latency from 280ms → 2.1s. correlates with CPU spikes on gpu-host-37.

maya: repro steps: send a few concurrent requests, tail shows repeated OOM-like eviction messages in inference container. attaching snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T03:41:12Z] eviction: cached-kv overflow, evicting 128MB
[2026-03-15T03:41:13Z] runtime: failed to allocate scratch for attention kernel
[2026-03-15T03:41:14Z] inference: request dropped, reason=kernel-init-failure
```

tia: @jordan can you confirm autoscaler didn't do something weird? I see pods are at desired count but node CPU is pinned.

jordan: autoscaler stable. no recent scaling events. nodes are at full capacity because one pod is thrashing GPU memory and causing host-level swapping. looking at `kubectl -n inference describe pod gpu-hosted-37` shows frequent restarts of the container.

pd-bot: Secondary missed ack within policy window. Manager escalation to @ops-manager fired and phone call attempted. Manager was paged at 03:49 UTC.

ops-manager: I got the call and joined the bridge. quick question — is this limited to a single host or wider?

noah: so far only gpu-host-37 shows the eviction/alloc failures. other hosts stable. seems like a corrupted model shard or runaway KV cache growth for a particular tenant.

maya: mitigation plan in progress: 1) cordon gpu-host-37 2) drain pods with graceful timeout 30s 3) route traffic away from region-us-west-2 to us-east-1 temporary 4) restart model server with cleared KV cache and a lower max_cache_size env var.

sam: pushing a temporary routing rule now: `redwood-routes set --service hosted-inference-prod --region us-west-2 --weight 0.2` to shift 80% traffic away from us-west-2. will monitor errors.

incident-bot: @maya marked the incident as 'investigating'. Bridge: https://meet.redwood/bridge/INC-20260315-17 (joined by maya, noah, ops-manager).

maya: cordon/drain done on gpu-host-37: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-37 && kubectl drain gpu-host-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30` — pods evicted. restarting model-server with `MAX_KV_CACHE=256MB`.

noah: restarted instance looks better, initial healthcheck green. tailing logs now. latency starting to normalize in metrics.

sam: post-mitigation traffic: error rate dropped to 0.4% in us-west-2; overall p50 latency back to 320ms. marking customer impact as "partial degradation" for ~15 minutes.

tia: can we lock this to a hotfix? model-hosting team should run a diagnostic on KV cache growth; possible fix: enforce per-model cache limit and fail-fast on allocation errors.

ops-manager: agreed. action items:
- maya: generate incident timeline + gather logs (INC-20260315-17)
- noah: run diagnostic on model shard / tenancy on gpu-host-37 and check for corrupted checkpoint usage
- jordan: add a node-level OOM alert that triggers before cpu > 90% (sensitive threshold)
- sam: revert routing weight back to normal only after 30m of stable metrics

maya: starting a quick postmortem doc draft. initial RCA hypothesis: runaway KV cache growth on a specific model instance caused repeated allocation failures at kernel init, which led to request drops and elevated latencies; autoscaler didn't preempt because pod CPU stayed stable but GPU memory pressure was the key signal missed.

pd-bot: Incident acknowledged by @maya at 03:52 UTC. PagerDuty incident status: acknowledged -> in_progress.

noah: one more note — we observed a minor spike in cold-start kernel loads after the restart; may want to schedule a warmup cron to prefill caches overnight.

maya: handing off to on-call tomorrow morning @noah. I'll finish logs and leave notes in the incident doc.

ops-manager: good job triaging. we'll keep this incident open for a full RCA. tagging SRE-ml and model-hosting teams.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-17 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. next update requested in 2h or when RCA draft is available. :white_check_mark:
